name: Elizabethan and Jacobean Period
description: The literature of England from the accession of Elizabeth I to the death of James I: the flowering of the sonnet vogue and of Spenser's allegorical epic, the rise of the commercial public theatre with Marlowe, Kyd, and Shakespeare, the prose experiments of Lyly, Greene, Nashe, and Deloney, the discovery literature of Hakluyt, Ralegh, and Purchas, the metaphysical lyric of Donne, and the Jacobean tragedy and city comedy of Webster, Middleton, and Jonson. It closes with the Caroline accession of 1625.
